title: Modified K-means Algorithm with Local Optimality Guarantees
summary: The paper shows that Lloyd's K-means need not converge to a locally optimal solution, giving a counterexample and distinguishing discrete (D-local) and continuous (C-local) optimality. It proposes LO-K-means, which adds post-convergence verification/repair steps (C-LO, D-LO, or Min-D-LO) to K-means while preserving the same per-iteration time complexity. Experiments on synthetic and real data show that D-LO and Min-D-LO reduce clustering loss relative to K-means, with Min-D-LO giving mean clustering loss 57.32 on Iris K=5 with random initialization.

match_target.why: This is the user's hinted target and the cheapest direct demonstration of the paper's central loss-reduction result: Iris has only 150 points and 4 dimensions, 20 runs are reported at under 0.001 s each, and Min-D-LO is the variant the paper highlights as the best accuracy/time tradeoff.

tolerance.why: Rule 4: clustering loss is an unbounded loss; the paper reports a variance (9.83) rather than a standard deviation, so Rule 1's 3-std band is not directly applicable. A 10% relative band is 5.732 loss units around 57.32.

data.name: Iris
data.how_to_get: Use sklearn.datasets.load_iris or the UCI Iris dataset; N=150, d=4.

data.name: Wine Quality
data.how_to_get: Use the UCI Wine Quality dataset (Cortez et al., 2009); N=6,497, d=11.

data.name: News20-1 and News20-2
data.how_to_get: Use scikit-learn's 20 newsgroups loader; News20-1 is the first 2,000 instances with 1,089 features whose word frequencies are between 2% and 80%; News20-2 is the first 200 instances with 131,017 features.

data.name: Yeast
data.how_to_get: Use the UCI Yeast dataset (Nakai & Kanehisa); N=1,484, d=8.
